<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Biomass-derived porous carbons are promising candidates for supercapacitor electrodes due to their high surface area, tunable pore structures, and superior conductivity. In this study, peanut shells were utilized as a sustainable precursor to synthesize hierarchical porous carbon via H
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    PO
                    <jats:sub>4</jats:sub>
                    activation. The resulting materials feature a well-defined micro-mesoporous architecture, achieving a specific capacitance of 221.9 F g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    at 0.5 A g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    in a three-electrode configuration. Furthermore, the symmetric supercapacitor demonstrated exceptional long-term durability, with 99.3% capacitance retention over 20 000 cycles at 10 A g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    . These findings offer a scalable and efficient strategy for converting agricultural waste into high-performance energy storage materials.
                  </jats:p>
title: Porous carbon materials from peanut shells for high-rate and long-cycle supercapacitors
